# pglite-cipher

> Encryption at rest for PGlite (Postgres in the browser and in webviews), like SQLCipher for SQLite. It is a PGlite filesystem (`EncryptedFs`) that encrypts every file under PGDATA with AES-256-GCM through WebCrypto, stores the blocks in IndexedDB, hides file names and sizes, and detects tampering at open. No runtime dependencies; `@electric-sql/pglite` (^0.5.10) is a peer dependency. While the database is open, its contents are plaintext in memory.

To add it to an app that already uses PGlite, read llms-full.txt: it is self-contained.

## Docs

- [llms-full.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/2002Bishwajeet/pglite-cipher/main/llms-full.txt): everything an agent needs to integrate it, in one file
- [README](https://github.com/2002Bishwajeet/pglite-cipher/blob/main/README.md): what it is and a quick start
- [Guides](https://github.com/2002Bishwajeet/pglite-cipher/blob/main/docs/guides/README.md): quick start, migrating an existing app, where to keep the key, rotation, errors and recovery
- [Usage](https://github.com/2002Bishwajeet/pglite-cipher/blob/main/docs/usage.md): options, syncing, open modes, errors, keys and rotation, verify(), memory on mobile
- [Security](https://github.com/2002Bishwajeet/pglite-cipher/blob/main/SECURITY.md): threat model and primitives
